metadata.scenario: A prospect calls to dispute a consultation fee that was supposed to be waived as per their understanding. Category: Billing. Flags: billing_dispute. Customer type: prospect.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret speaking. How can I assist you today? Hi Margaret, this is Rose Patterson. I’m calling regarding a consultation fee that I thought was waived. Hi Rose, it’s nice to hear from you. Can you provide me with more details about the consultation? Yes, I was under the impression that since I’ve been a client for over 18 months, the consultation fee would be waived for any additional services. I understand your concern. Let me check your account details to clarify that for you. One moment, please… Okay, I see that you have been receiving companion care and personal assistance regularly. However, the consultation fee is typically charged for initial assessments of new services. But I was told when I started that as a long-term client, those fees would be waived. I’m really frustrated. I completely understand, Rose, and I’m really sorry for any confusion. Let me review the notes from your initial intake. It looks like I don’t see any indication that the fee would be waived. However, I can escalate this to our billing department to see if there are exceptions we can make for you. I’d appreciate that, but I just want to be clear. I shouldn’t have to pay if I was promised a waiver. Of course, I can assure you that we will take your concerns seriously. I’ll also ensure that your son is included in this conversation since he manages your care coordination. Would you like me to reach out to him directly? Yes, please. His number is on file. Perfect, I’ll make a note of that. Once I gather more information, I’ll provide you with an update as soon as possible. Thank you, Margaret. I just want clarity on this. I don’t want to be charged for something I was told wouldn’t cost me. Absolutely, Rose. I’ll look into this thoroughly. Additionally, if you’re considering any new services, let me know, and I can discuss promotional offers we have available. I might be interested in more assistance for my mother. I’ll think about that while we sort this out. That sounds great! I’ll reach out with an update by the end of the week. Thank you, Margaret. I really appreciate your help. You’re very welcome, Rose. Take care, and I look forward to speaking with you soon. Bye! Goodbye!
